headline: AlphaSMO brings $45T in institutional finance data to AI agents
summary: New MCP server processes SEC 13F filings and insider trading data, offering AI agents direct access to real-time financial intelligence.
details: AlphaSMO is a new platform that transforms SEC 13F filings, the quarterly reports from institutional investors managing over $100M, into clean, queryable data for AI agents. This effectively provides "Bloomberg Terminal data, but for AI agents," enabling them to access live financial intelligence instead of relying on hallucinated or outdated information.

The AlphaSMO MCP server exposes seven tools that AI agents can call directly. This allows agents to query legally mandated disclosures from over 5,000 institutional investors managing more than $45 trillion in assets, providing a direct window into real-world financial markets.

Raw 13F filings are complex and unreadable without processing. AlphaSMO bridges this gap by making this data accessible through a single function call for AI agents. The platform uniquely combines institutional 13F data with insider trading signals into a single "convergence signal," indicating when both smart money and company insiders are buying.

Users can ask their AI agents specific questions like "Show me Berkshire Hathaway's latest 13F holdings" or "Are insiders buying or selling NVDA?" Each query triggers a real API call, ensuring accurate and up-to-date responses. The platform is built with the official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and supports both TypeScript and Python MCP clients.

Anonymous access is available with IP-based rate limiting, and free API keys can be obtained at alphasmo.com/developer to raise limits. AlphaSMO aims to provide AI agents with the tools to accurately understand smart money movements, moving beyond guesswork and stale data.

headline_marked: [[Warner Bros. sues Amazon]] for allegedly poaching employees, calling it a 'lawless shopping spree'
headline: Warner Bros. sues Amazon for allegedly poaching employees, calling it a 'lawless shopping spree'
summary: Warner Bros. Discovery claims Amazon is illegally hiring its staff, including a former senior VP, by offering higher pay and legal support.
details: Warner Bros. Discovery has filed a lawsuit against Amazon, accusing the tech giant of engaging in a "lawless employee shopping spree." The suit specifically names Pia Barlow, former senior VP for originals marketing at Warner Bros., as one of the key employees allegedly poached.

The complaint states that Amazon "has chosen to ride on the coattails of other well-established Hollywood mainstays." Barlow was reportedly under contract until October 31st, 2027, but is set to begin a new role as Amazon's head of original series marketing on August 3rd.

Warner Bros. alleges that Amazon knowingly "induced" Barlow to breach her contract by offering a superior compensation package and legal backing. The lawsuit suggests these poaching efforts are ongoing and part of a broader strategy by Amazon to break into the entertainment industry.

This legal battle highlights a growing tension between traditional entertainment companies and tech firms expanding into media. Similar disputes have occurred previously, such as YouTube's settlement with Disney over hiring a veteran executive and 20th Century Fox winning a lawsuit against Netflix for poaching two executives.
